question.problem: A particle $P$ moves along a counterclockwise circular path centered at $O$ in the $xy$-plane with a constant angular velocity of $4\,\text{rad/s}.$ Given that the particle is located at $(2,0)$ when $t=0,$ find the velocity of the particle at $t=\frac{\pi }{4}$ seconds.
question.worked_solution:
The position function of a particle moving in a circular path of radius $R$ in the $xy$-plane with a constant angular velocity $\omega $ is given by

$$
r(t)=R(\operatorname{cos}⁡\omega t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡\omega t\,j),
$$

where it is assumed that the circle is centered at $O,$ and the particle is at the position $(R,0)$ when $t=0.$

In our case, we have $R=2$ and $\omega =4\text{ rad/s},$ so we get that the position function is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =2(\operatorname{cos}⁡4t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡4t\,j).\end{aligned}
$$

We find the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =(2(\operatorname{cos}⁡4t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡4t\,j))^{′} \\  & =-8\operatorname{sin}⁡4t\,i+8\operatorname{cos}⁡4t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we find the velocity vector at $t=\frac{\pi }{4},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =-8\operatorname{sin}⁡(4\cdot \frac{\pi }{4})\,i+8\operatorname{cos}⁡(4\cdot \frac{\pi }{4})\,j \\  & =-8\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi \,i+8\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi \,j \\  & =-8\,j\end{aligned}
$$
